crime: When {WITCH_NAME} was small, she threw the ball too hard once too often. After that, her classmates passed it around the circle, over her open hands, until the bell rang. "When they stop throwing to you," she said, "it's already decided." From that day on, she kept a stone hidden in her pocket.

In the mansion, one of the prisoners sat by the fountain in the courtyard every dusk and posted a bedtime question to the group chat, the kind she used to ask her sisters before they fell asleep. {WITCH_NAME} answered from the upper railing, always last, a beat late, after the chat had moved on.
One night after dusk, the girl at the fountain sent her a private message: "You don't have to answer the bedtime questions. It's fine just to read."

{WITCH_NAME} looked down into the dark courtyard. The only light was the girl's face, lit by her screen as she waited for a reply. {WITCH_NAME} fixed her eyes on that lit temple and threw the stone. Like anything she threw, it flew to the spot her eyes held, and the light dropped from the girl's face.

The prisoners found the girl slumped on the rim of the fountain, a stone beside her, her phone dark in her lap. Afterward they stood at the upper railing after dusk and could not make out the fountain below. In the trial court, they ruled that a hand right beside her had struck the blow: from any farther off, no one could have seen her in that dark, not even {WITCH_NAME}.

Then one prisoner woke the dead girl's phone. It opened on her message to {WITCH_NAME}, the reply box still empty. The prisoners understood. The girl had sat there waiting with her screen lit, the one light the railing could see, and {WITCH_NAME} could hit anything she could see.
fields.epitaph: The only light she ever threw at was someone waiting for her answer.
fields.epithet: The Girl the Ball Went Around
execution: The execution stand raises a ring of iron schoolgirls around a post. She is chained to the post, her hands bound open in front of her. The iron girls throw an iron ball around the ring, over her open hands, round and round, never to her. Then they turn inward and throw every iron ball to her, too hard, through her open hands and into her chest, one after another. She hangs still on the post, her hands still open above the iron balls heaped at her feet.

magic.name: Dead Eye
magic.text: Anything she throws lands exactly where her eyes are fixed, curving around whatever is in the way.
